newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing investors open fewer stock accounts in May.
newsitem.headline: Beijing investors open fewer stock accounts in May.

text.p: Investors in China's capital, Beijing, opened fewer stock trading accounts in May compared with the previous month due to government efforts to cool the stock markets, the Financial News said on Thursday.

Since 22 May, the average daily number of accounts opened by institutional investors fell by 37.9 percent from an average of 22.3 a day in April, it said, quoting the local securities registration corporation.
In May alone, individual investors opened 51,875 new accounts, falling 8.8 percent while institutional investors opened 382 accounts, down 14.3 percent compared with the previous month, it said.
China imposed curbs on the trading of shares by state-owned and listed companies on 22 May.
Total accounts opened by residents in the capital reached 840,697 by the end-May, it said.
